title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
description:
You are given a string `s` consisting of uppercase English letters and an integer `k`. You can choose any character in the string and replace it with any other uppercase English letter, performing this operation at most `k` times.

Return the length of the longest contiguous substring containing all identical letters that can be obtained after performing at most `k` character replacements.
constraints: s consists of only uppercase English letters ('A'-'Z').
hints: For any window [left..right], the minimum number of replacements needed to make all characters equal is (window length) - (frequency of the most common character in the window).
Use a sliding window with a 26-element frequency array. Whenever window_len - max_freq > k, advance left by 1.
You do not need to recompute max_freq when shrinking left: the window only needs to grow past the best valid length found so far, which requires an even larger frequency.

examples.explanation: Replace the two 'A's with 'B's (or two 'B's with 'A's) to obtain a uniform string of length 4.
Replace the middle 'A' in "AABABBA" to form "AABBBBA", giving a repeating substring "BBBB" of length 4.
With k = 0 replacements allowed and all distinct letters, the longest uniform substring has length 1.
